title: Potential recovery from first positive-time passage observations
known: A finite connected labelled undirected graph X with at least two vertices
Symmetric conductances w_xy, positive exactly on edges, and positive masses mu_x
A nonempty proper observed set B
A fixed known h > 0 and finite integer observation horizon T >= 1
unknown: q:X→R with q(x) >= 0 and h(r(x)+q(x)) <= 1 at every vertex; r(x)=sum_y w_xy/mu_x. Only q is unknown.
kernel: K_q(x,y)=h*w_xy/mu_x for x != y; K_q(x,x)=1-h(r(x)+q(x)). Missing row mass h*q(x) goes to an absorbing cemetery state.
observations: Exact F_xy(n)=P_x(tau_y=n), x,y in B, 1 <= n <= T, where tau_y=inf{n>=1:X_n=y}. Visits to other observed vertices are allowed before hitting y. Holding at x counts as a one-step return when x=y. These are first-passage probabilities, not occupancy probabilities or first returns to the set B.
question: For which graph, observed-set and horizon conditions is q mapped to {F_xy(n)} injective? Under sufficient conditions, construct a recovery procedure; otherwise exhibit distinct admissible potentials with identical specified observations.
success: A precisely scoped identifiability/reconstruction theorem with proof
Or a checked nonidentifiability counterexample satisfying the frozen assumptions
excluded: Occupancy data substituted for first-passage data
Automatic transfer of benchmark winners into hidden-q runs
formalization: Not formalized. Existing diagonal algebra proves recovery only on B. No sufficiency claim for hidden vertices or finite T is asserted.
change_policy: Changes require a new contract version; benchmark jobs never modify or execute this research reference.
